Best iPhone planning apps for automatic task rescheduling

FlowSavvy and Motion are the strongest starting points if you want tasks to automatically move around meetings rather than repeatedly dragging calendar blocks yourself. But they serve different needs: FlowSavvy emphasizes straightforward personal scheduling, while Motion offers a more elaborate system for priorities, deadlines, projects, and teams.

There are also useful alternatives, particularly Reclaim AI, SkedPal, and Sunsama. The important distinction is between an app that continuously rebuilds your schedule and one that merely helps you place tasks on your calendar.

Automatic scheduling means the app chooses task times based on your constraints. Assisted scheduling means it can suggest or place blocks, but you retain more responsibility for rearranging the plan.

2. FlowSavvy vs Motion
FlowSavvy

Best for straightforward automatic time blocking

FlowSavvy places flexible tasks into available time, splits longer tasks, balances workload, and recalculates when plans change. Fixed meetings and fixed-time tasks are not automatically moved.

Its iOS app is described as fully featured, making it particularly suitable if you mainly plan from an iPhone. 
App Store
+1

Key scheduling limits

Free: schedules up to 2 weeks ahead, with one scheduling-hours profile and three repeating auto-scheduled tasks.

Pro: schedules up to 8 weeks ahead, with unlimited scheduling profiles, recurring auto-scheduled tasks, priorities, and dependencies.

Tasks due beyond the scheduling cutoff remain unscheduled until they enter the window.

Neither plan can create time that doesn't exist; overcommitment warnings help identify deadline problems.

Official sources: Pricing and limits · Scheduling cutoff explained

Motion

Best for complex workloads and deadline management

Motion schedules tasks using duration, priority, start dates, deadlines, available hours, and meetings. When a meeting changes, it can automatically reshuffle flexible work and warn when deadlines are at risk.

Its iPhone app is explicitly a companion to the web/desktop product, and certain settings require a computer. 
App Store
+1

Key scheduling limits

Requires a paid subscription after its trial.

Tasks need realistic durations, priorities, and deadlines for useful scheduling.

Task splitting depends on chunking rules; without them, Motion seeks a full uninterrupted slot.

Manually placed fixed tasks do not automatically move.

External calendar events sync differently from tasks; don't assume every task created in another calendar imports as a Motion task.

Official sources: How auto-scheduling works · Scheduling models and constraints

Practical difference: FlowSavvy is a better first trial for someone who wants to enter tasks on an iPhone and have them fitted around appointments. Motion becomes more attractive when the planner also needs to coordinate multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines.

3. Other suitable options and their limitations

Reclaim AI

Strong for protecting focus time, scheduling habits, adding meeting buffers, and automatically adjusting calendar commitments.

Its published free-plan scheduling range is 1 week, versus 8 weeks on the paid plan described in its pricing comparison. Mobile app parity with its web experience is not established by the official material reviewed, so verify your intended iPhone workflow before subscribing. 
Pick the right plan for you

Official features and plan limits

SkedPal

Particularly good for specifying preferred time windows, such as working on a report on weekday afternoons, and allowing the scheduler to find suitable blocks.

It supports flexible scheduling and task bundling. However, fixed-time plans generally stay fixed, and task changes may require pressing Update Schedule rather than immediately rebuilding the calendar. Its official planning documentation does not establish complete iPhone feature parity.

Official planning guide

Sunsama

A middle ground between manual time blocking and automation. You can drag tasks into the calendar or use an auto-schedule command. Optional settings shift tasks when conflicts occur or when work finishes early.

The important limitation: its scheduler only considers calendar events currently in view, and it may need your decision when there isn't enough free time.

Structured

A polished iPhone-oriented visual timeline, with AI-assisted scheduling and replanning available in Pro.

It is not the same as a continuously self-adjusting task scheduler. Replan lets you decide what to do with unfinished tasks, while Structured AI can make requested scheduling changes. Its iPhone app currently requires iOS 18 or later.

Illustrative example, not an actual schedule generated by any app.

The automation advantage is substantial when meetings change frequently. However, no scheduling algorithm guarantees that every task will fit before its deadline. Available working hours, minimum task-block duration, calendar visibility, and scheduling windows all matter.

5. Which should you choose?

Best overall for iPhone-first planning

FlowSavvy

Start with its free plan. It has genuine automatic rescheduling, calendar integrations, and a usable two-week scheduling horizon.

Top pick

Choose Motion instead if deadline pressure, competing priorities, and complex projects matter more than having a fully standalone iPhone experience.

Choose Reclaim AI if your biggest problem is meetings consuming your focus time, especially when you already manage tasks elsewhere.

Choose SkedPal if you want detailed control over when different kinds of work are allowed to happen.

Choose Sunsama or Structured if you prefer consciously planning your day and only want automation to help with adjustments.

What to test before paying

Try this exact scenario in your preferred app: connect your real meeting calendar, create a two-hour flexible task due tomorrow, and then add a meeting during its scheduled slot. Check whether the task moves automatically, whether it splits into sensible blocks, whether the new plan appears on your iPhone, and whether the app warns you when the deadline becomes impossible.

That test will reveal more than a product's use of the term AI scheduling.

Bottom line: For the specific requirement of automatically rescheduling tasks around meetings on an iPhone, I would trial FlowSavvy first and Motion second. Their automatic scheduling behavior is well documented, and the distinction in mobile functionality is significant.

Comparison based on official product, help-center, pricing, and developer-published App Store documentation available in October 2026. Features, prices, and platform support can change.
